Use case: precise-object-edit. TWO references: Image 1 is the ORIGINAL portrait and is authoritative for POSE, HAND POSITIONS except the requested hand, FACE, LARGE HEADPIECE SCALE and BACK-TURNED body. Image 2 is a rejected edit: use ONLY its readable red scarf/waist-sash attachment design; DO NOT copy its bent arm on image-left or small horn-like headpiece.
CRITICAL USER CORRECTION — WHICH HAND: The user means the CHARACTER'S LEFT HAND, which is on the RIGHT SIDE OF THE IMAGE, currently hanging beside/behind the hip holding the lower crescent weapon. Change ONLY THIS IMAGE-RIGHT ARM/HAND pose. The outstretched arm and weapon on the LEFT SIDE OF THE IMAGE must stay extended exactly as in Image 1. Do NOT bend or lower that image-left arm as Image 2 did. The body stays in Image 1's exact rear-three-quarter BACK-TURNED look-back stance, same legs and feet, head turned back over shoulder; no front-facing rotation.
REPOSITION IMAGE-RIGHT / CHARACTER LEFT ARM: lift the formerly hanging image-right hand to a relaxed bent-elbow position beside the right edge of the WAIST, with the elbow lower than the hand and the forearm angled gently up and out away from the hip. The upper arm naturally follows the far side of the torso; the left wrist and hand sit clearly OUTSIDE the body silhouette on image-right at waist level, not behind the buttock, not touching the shorts. Hold the second crescent blade upright/diagonal outside the waist, lower than shoulder height. No stiff straight arm or backwards broken wrist. Keep that weapon clear of torso and cloth.
LEFT HAND ACCURACY: this IMAGE-RIGHT hand must be drawn as a genuine anatomical LEFT hand, not a right hand mirrored at the wrong wrist. Use a natural slightly supinated grip with the palm's thenar/thumb base partly visible so handedness is readable; one thumb arising from the radial side of this LEFT wrist, index beside it, four fingers naturally curled around the blunt inner handle. Correct palm/back-of-hand relation through wrist and forearm rotation. No reversed thumb, duplicate thumb, extra fingers or fused hand. Exactly two arms and two hands, one hand per weapon. Keep the image-left hand's original placement while avoiding anatomical defects.
HEADPIECE — USER REJECTED SMALL HORN DIADEM: Keep a LARGE, elegant, wide black-and-gold crescent ceremonial HAT, roughly as broad as the original headpiece in Image 1. It must have a readable shallow BLACK LACQUER HAT CROWN seated on the head, a continuous sweeping WIDE GOLDEN CRESCENT BRIM, and coherent attachment between crown and brim. It is glamorous Japanese fantasy millinery. One integrated dramatic sideways-swept crescent silhouette, not several floating blades. REMOVE the small vertical crescent/horn sitting on top of the forehead from Image 2; no upright bull horns, no horned demon crown, no tiny tiara. Keep broad graceful sideways and backward gold curves, restrained red fastening at the back of the hat. Face unobscured, hat fully inside frame.
RED FABRIC LOGIC from Image 2: preserve the bold beautiful red/black balance with ONE crimson scarf secured by a visible gold clasp at the back/side collar, TWO broad tails trailing together behind shoulder toward image-left. A separate crimson sash threads under the waist belt and has ONE visible side knot with TWO broad tails descending behind hips and trailing in the SAME wind direction. Each red strip traces to an actual fastening. Four broad fabric ends, no independent ribbon loops, no ribbons emerging from hair or weapons. Keep the black/gold overskirt clearly attached at the waist. Clean intact hems, broad folds, enough empty space around both hands.
Preserve Image 1's delicate Japanese anime face/red eyes, adult feminine identity, long black hair, black rear-view combat shorts fully covering hips, black thigh boots, gold armor, pose/camera, pale grey plain background. Full body 1024x1536. Do not rotate hips to front. No scenery, particles, noise, rough ragged edges, text, watermark or extra character. Priority: correct image-right hand only; original outstretched image-left arm unchanged; large structured non-horned hat; physically attached red cloth.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this EXISTING finished Japanese-anime adult female red-black-gold crescent warrior. Preserve the exact BACK-TURNED rear-three-quarter hip/body direction, looking back over the same shoulder, same face/red eyes, same leg stance, black hair, black fitted shorts and thigh boots, and two golden crescent weapons. Do NOT rotate the body to face front. Keep delicate Japanese anime face, pale grey simple background, 1024x1536 full-body portrait, complete feet and weapon tips with margins.
USER FIX 1 — LEFT ARM / LEFT HAND: the arm currently stretched stiffly toward image-left must be repositioned. This is the character's ANATOMICAL LEFT arm, not a right arm. Lower that upper arm naturally beside her left ribs, elbow softly bent about 90 degrees at her left waist, forearm angled diagonally forward and slightly out toward image-left. Left hand now holds its crescent blade beside the LEFT HIP/WAIST, below the chest, with clear space from the torso and hanging cloth. Show a relaxed anatomically valid LEFT-handed grip on a blunt dark handle attached inside the crescent. Construct the left hand from the left forearm: one thumb on the radial side, index adjacent to it, middle/ring/little fingers wrapping in their proper order, knuckles and palm consistent with forearm rotation. Do not mirror a right hand onto the left wrist. The visible back-of-hand can face partly toward the camera, wrist straight and relaxed. Make the thumb and four fingers legible instead of a tangle. Exactly two shoulders, two arms and two hands. Keep the other arm and blade naturally down on image-right as in the reference. No extra or floating hands, blades do not touch fingers or body.
USER FIX 2 — HEADPIECE: replace the confusing pile of gigantic overlapping gold crescents with ONE readable elegant golden crescent diadem, attached to a clearly visible slim black-and-gold headband encircling the crown of her head. A single modest crescent crest sits centered on the band, above the forehead. It is wearable jewelry, not a huge hat, not a floating weapon, not several stacked crescents. Preserve some hair volume and the face. Minimal side attachments, clean continuous shape, no confusing floating shards.
USER FIX 3 — RED FABRIC CONSTRUCTION: retain the beautiful dramatic red/black balance, but use physically connected, readable garments. A single crimson scarf fastens at the back/side collar with a small gold clasp; its TWO broad tails flow together behind the left shoulder in the same gentle wind direction. A separate crimson waist sash is threaded under the existing gold waist belt, tied with one visible side knot; its TWO broader tails descend from that knot behind the hips, flowing in the same direction as the scarf. Thus FOUR broad red fabric ends total, each visibly traceable to collar or belt. No detached strips, no endless looping ribbon, no ribbons growing out of hair, hands or weapons, no arbitrary crisscross red bands over thighs. Preserve the elegant black/gold side overskirt as separate structured cloth attached to the belt. Use a few broad folds, intact hems, restrained gold trim; leave negative space so both hands and each weapon are easy to read. Keep a graceful amount of flowing red fabric without making the picture busy.
Finish: refined clean Japanese anime rendering, clean silhouette, no noisy micro-detail, ragged fringe, spikes everywhere, particles, scenery, grain, text, watermark or extra person. Only these targeted changes; retain the character's BACK-TURNED look-back stance throughout.
